# `antizenith()` {#fn-antizenith}

A05 verified the geometric anti-zenith declination and tropical-boundary eligibility at two epochs. [A05 results](a05-solar-limits.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-antizenith)

```{=html}
<p>The direction opposite the zenith corresponds geometrically to minus the site latitude.
Build 2.0.9009 tests the site against the obliquity at the requested epoch. At the geometric anti-zenith, parallax vanishes. It
returns NULL outside that band. This is a target declination for comparison with
orientations, not an observable solar transit below ground.
</p>
```

**Interpretation and limits.** Record the site's latitude and the epoch and parallax assumptions used for a solar limit. A returned limit is a geometrical target; an observer still needs an independent reason to regard it as culturally significant.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>loc</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>This can be either the latitude of the
location, or a <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> object.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>parallax</code></th><td><code>0.00224</code></td><td><p>Mean horizontal parallax in degrees. The default is 0.00224 degrees for the Sun.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>altitude</code></th><td><code>-90</code></td><td><p>Altitude in degrees used for the approximate parallax correction. The geometric default is -90 degrees.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>year</code></th><td><code>skyscapeR.env$cur.year</code></td><td><p>Astronomical year used to calculate the obliquity and hence the tropical latitude limit.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>Solar declination in degrees with the requested parallax correction, or NULL when the latitude falls outside the solstitial limits used by the function.
</p>
```

</details>
